statica-constructio.translation: Geometric proof and construction by point-weights alone, without auxiliary circles or lines
statica-constructio.definition: Ceva's signature methodological innovation ('substitutisque linearum vice ponderibus... nulla adhibita circulorum, linearumque praevia constructione... solis ponderibus statice enodare'): replacing auxiliary Euclidean lines and circles with hypothetical Archimedean weights placed at vertices so that collinearity and concurrency follow immediately from the uniqueness of the center of gravity.

centrum-gravitatis.translation: Unique equilibrium point P = (uA + vB + wC)/(u + v + w) of a weighted configuration
centrum-gravitatis.definition: By Ceva's Axiomata I–II and Petitio, every system of commensurable or incommensurable point weights admits a single determinate center of gravity, and grouping subsets of weights by their partial fulcrums (e.g., balancing B and C at D first, then balancing v + w at D against u at A) must always pass through the same global center P.

momentum-ponderis.translation: Product of weight and lever arm: u · AF = v · FB (A : B = BF : FA)
momentum-ponderis.definition: The Archimedean inverse-proportion law of the straight lever (Equiponderants I.6–7): two weights u at A and v at B balance around fulcrum F on line AB if and only if AF / FB = v / u.

pondus-negativum.headword: pondus subtractivum / F - A (algebraic negative weight)
pondus-negativum.translation: Analytic negative weight ('more analytico, seu algebrico F - A') governing exterior concurrency
pondus-negativum.language: Neo-Latin (Liber Primus, Elementum III & p. 5 Scholium)
pondus-negativum.definition: When three cevians concur at an exterior point P outside triangle ABC, one vertex carries an upward/subtractive weight ('pondus... more analytico, seu algebrico ita scribemus F - A, hoc est F minus A'), placing two fulcrums externally on the extended sides so that two negative directed side ratios multiply with one positive ratio to +1—anticipating Möbius's signed barycentric coordinates (1827) by 149 years.

obelus-additio.translation: Ludovico Monza's 1678 typographic dagger symbol denoting algebraic addition (+)
obelus-additio.definition: As explained in the printer's prefatory note to the 1678 Milan quarto, Ludovico Monza's press set compound static sums with the obelus/dagger '†' (e.g., 'A † F' = A + F at an interior fulcrum) paired with the analytic minus sign '-' ('F - A') for exterior fulcrums.

ratio-composita.language: Latin (Euclid VI / Commandino / Clavius / Ceva Props. VII–VIII)
ratio-composita.definition: Classical Euclidean expression for the product of ratios ('ratio ex rationibus composita'): in Liber Primus, Props. VII–VIII, Ceva cites Commandino and Clavius to translate static weight elimination (v/u) · (w/v) · (u/w) = 1 into the pure compound-ratio equality of side segments.

ceviana.translation: Straight line joining a polygon or polyhedron vertex to a point on the opposite side or face
ceviana.definition: Coined in nineteenth-century triangle geometry in honor of Giovanni Ceva: any line AD, BE, CF joining a vertex of triangle ABC to a finite point on the opposite sideline (interior or extended).

sectio-harmonica.translation: Collinear quadruple (B, C; D, D') with cross-ratio -1 where D' = EF ∩ BC
sectio-harmonica.language: Latin / Projective Geometry (Liber Primus, Elementum I & Props. VII–VIII)
sectio-harmonica.definition: When AD, BE, CF concur at P (BD/DC = w/v), the dual Menelaus transversal EF meets sideline BC at D' with directed ratio BD'/D'C = -w/v, so (B, C; D, D') = -1—furnishing a straightedge-only construction of harmonic conjugates.

coniugatum-isotomicum.translation: Reciprocal-weight concurrency P* = (u⁻¹ : v⁻¹ : w⁻¹) obtained by reflecting cevian feet across side midpoints
coniugatum-isotomicum.language: Latin / Triangle Geometry (Liber Secundus, Prop. I Corollarium)
coniugatum-isotomicum.definition: If AD, BE, CF concur at P, reflecting D, E, F across the midpoints of BC, CA, AB yields D*, E*, F* with BD* = DC, CE* = EA, AF* = FB; each side ratio inverts, preserving the unit product 1⁻¹ = 1 and proving concurrency at P* (notably mapping Gergonne X(7) to Nagel X(8)).

punctum-contactus.translation: Concurrency center of cevians joining vertices to the contact points of an inscribed circle or ellipse
punctum-contactus.language: Latin / Triangle Geometry (Liber Secundus, Prop. I)
punctum-contactus.definition: Proved in Ceva's Liber Secundus, Proposition I (1678)—more than a century before Gergonne—both for a triangle circumscribed about a circle (weights 1/(s-a) : 1/(s-b) : 1/(s-c)) and for a triangle circumscribed about any ellipse.

quadrilaterum-non-planum.headword: quadrilaterum non in eodem plano (3D skew quadrilateral)
quadrilaterum-non-planum.translation: Non-planar spatial four-bar cycle whose four weighted side fulcrums are coplanar and opposite-concurrent
quadrilaterum-non-planum.language: Neo-Latin (Liber Primus, Elementum V Corollarium, pp. 6–7)
quadrilaterum-non-planum.definition: Ceva's striking observation ('licet praedictum sic sectum quadrilaterum non in eodem plano iaceat') that four weights on a non-planar 3D quadrilateral produce four edge fulcrums in cyclic ratio product 1 whose two opposite-edge joins intersect in space at the global center of gravity O.

concordia-septem-linearum.headword: mira concordia septem linearum (7-line tetrahedral concurrency)
concordia-septem-linearum.translation: Simultaneous spatial concurrency of 4 vertex-face cevians and 3 skew-edge bimedians at O
concordia-septem-linearum.language: Neo-Latin (Liber Primus, Prop. XXIII, pp. 36–39, Tab. 3 Fig. 28)
concordia-septem-linearum.definition: For four non-zero weights (m_A, m_B, m_C, m_D) on a tetrahedron ABCD, the 4 lines joining each vertex to the static barycenter of its opposite face AND the 3 lines joining the fulcrums of opposite skew edges all concur ('mira quadam concordia') at the single 3D center of gravity O.

sectio-cylindrica.translation: Oblique plane section of a circular cylinder mapping circles to ellipses while preserving collinear ratios
sectio-cylindrica.language: Latin (Serenus / Borelli / Ceva Liber Secundus, Lemma I)
sectio-cylindrica.definition: In Liber Secundus, Lemma I (tab. 4, figs. 32–35), Ceva projects an n-gon circumscribed about a circular cylinder's base onto an oblique planar section (an ellipse), proving that collinear tangent-division ratios remain invariant.

ungula-cylindrica.translation: Solid wedge cut from a right circular cylinder by a plane through a base diameter (Vol = 2/3 R²H)
ungula-cylindrica.definition: Sliced parallel to the cylinder's axis and perpendicular to the base diameter, each cross-section of the cylindrical ungula is a right triangle proportional to R² - x², yielding exact volume (2/3) R²H—two-thirds of the circumscribed triangular prism without involving π.

indivisibilia-cautio.translation: Ceva's closing paradox demonstrating why naive parallel indivisibles fail on curved surfaces
indivisibilia-cautio.definition: At the close of the Appendix Geometrica, Ceva shows that summing parallel circular circumferences without accounting for the slant arc element ds = dz / cos(α) falsely equates curved surface areas (such as a sphere vs. a cone or cylinder), proving that Cavalieri's indivisibles require rigorous Archimedean frustum limits on surfaces.

spread-ceva.translation: Radical-free Rational Trigonometry formulation of Ceva's Theorem over Q
spread-ceva.definition: Replaces transcendental sine ratios sin(∠BAD)/sin(∠DAC) with rational vertex spreads s(∠BAD)/s(∠DAC) and segment lengths with quadrances Q(AF)/Q(FB), verifying Ceva's concurrency in 100% exact rational arithmetic with zero square roots.
